messages:
Samir K: :rotating_light: paging oncall, seeing a sudden spike in model errors + inflated latency for hosted/region-us-east. it started ~10m ago. logs show a ton of `kv_get` misses followed by 500s. @Priya can you pick this up?
IncidentBot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421. Severity: High. Pager: Priya N. Channel: #incidents.
Priya N: on it. quick glance at traces — a lot of requests hit a path that does `kv_cache.reuse=true` and then later `kv_cache.eviction` spikes. i'm worried about cross-request KV reuse.
Elena G: i just grabbed a sample trace, looks like seq offsets being applied incorrectly after a batch: logs:```
[13:02:11] req=abc seq_start=0 seq_end=128 kv_key=ctx-42 kv_seq=512
[13:02:11] req=def seq_start=0 seq_end=64 kv_key=ctx-42 kv_seq=384
[13:02:12] ERROR reuse mismatch: cached_seq=512 request_seq=0 --> mismatch
```
Samir K: that mismatch screams stale kv entries being reused across requests. any recent changes to continuous batching or the reuse policy?
Ivan P: rolled a batch-config change 22m ago to set `continuous_batching.batch_window_ms=8` and `kv_cache.reuse_enabled=true` (opt-in perf experiment).
Marta S: customer impact: Support reported 3 customers with garbled completions and some 502s — flagged as potential data leakage risk. we should assume high impact until proven otherwise.
Priya N: mitigation plan: 1) flip `kv_cache.reuse_enabled=false` for hosted default 2) if needed, temporarily increase `continuous_batching.batch_window_ms` to 20ms to reduce overlap 3) run a targeted cache evict for keys created in last 30m.
Samir K: do 1) ASAP. Ivan, can you flip the flag and push hotfix? include a quick rollback.
Ivan P: flipping flag now via rollout job: `redwood-config set --path /defaults/kv_cache/reuse_enabled false --env prod`
Ivan P: rollout at 13:07: applied to route: text-gen, region: us-east. monitoring...
Elena G: posting a quick probe to reproduce — sending high-concurrency workload with varying seq lengths.
Priya N: noticed immediate drop in 500s after flag flip. latency back to baseline in ~30s for most routes. still seeing a few error traces.
Samir K: start a targeted eviction for suspected keys. command:```
POST /admin/cache/evict
{ "prefix": "ctx-", "min_age_sec": 0, "max_age_sec": 3600 }
```
Ivan P: eviction kicked off 13:11. queued shards and evicted matching keys.
Marta S: reaching out to affected customers with initial statement: we observed degraded completions and are mitigating. ETA next update 30m.
Elena G: after eviction, probe runs show consistent seq offsets in logs. earlier samples showed `cached_seq` >> `request_seq` which is impossible unless reuse mapping ignored sequence resets.
Priya N: root cause hypothesis: reuse pooling reuses KV slots by key but doesn't reset per-request seq offsets when requests with different position offsets reuse same slot. this causes stale `kv_seq` to be applied to newer requests.
Ivan P: i dug into the pooling code — there's a fast-path that bypasses `seq_reset` for performance on hot path. added a quick guard locally and ran unit smoke: it fixes mismatch.
Samir K: for safety we rolled back reuse; next step is a code hotfix that preserves performance but enforces seq_reset. Ivan please open a PR and we can apply a canary.
Ivan P: PR opened: "fix(kv): reset seq on reuse guard" - #3247. planning a canary rollout to 5% tomorrow.
Marta S: ops note — customers that saw content corruption: acct-839, acct-412, acct-119. CS notified, we offered immediate mitigations and logs. legal has been looped for potential data leakage classification.
Priya N: current status: flag disabled, eviction done, errors down 98%, latency stable. moving to monitoring mode.
Elena G: add a regression test to the kernel test harness that replays mixed seq-length workloads with reuse enabled. simple unit tests missed this because they always used aligned seqs.
Samir K: agree. action items: [Priya] write incident timeline; [Ivan] submit PR + canary plan; [Elena] add tests + perf benchmark; [Marta] customer triage + msgs.
Priya N: creating incident ticket: INC-2026-0421-001 with timeline and root cause hypothesis. attaching traces and logs.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-0421 moved to postmortem-required. Owner: Priya N.
Marta S: follow-up: schedule a cross-team postmortem tomorrow 10:00am PT; invite eng-runtime, eng-ml, support, and security.
Samir K: thanks team. good catch on the reuse corner case. we'll keep this thread updated with PR link, canary results, and customer follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
